headline: 25 Aave V4 contracts catalogued on Ethereum: 3 Hubs, 11 Spokes, 11 Peripheral contracts (Access Manager, Configurators, Position Managers, Gateways, IR Strategies, Oracles); Ethereum-only at launch.

findings.text: Etherscan name-tag search via web_search returned the AAVE token (0x7fc66500c84a76ad7e9c93437bfc5ac33e2ddae9) and Aave V3 Pool addresses with name tags, but no V4-specific name-tagged addresses were surfaced from Etherscan search results. Direct fetch of Etherscan searchHandler for 'Aave V4' was not attempted due to fetch budget exhaustion; recorded as D1 partial.

Official deployments page at https://aave.com/docs/resources/addresses successfully fetched. Lists all Aave V4 deployed contracts on Ethereum: 3 Hubs (Core, Plus, Prime), 11 Spokes (Main, Bluechip, Ethena Correlated, Ethena Ecosystem, EtherFi eSpoke, Forex, Gold, Kelp eSpoke, Lido eSpoke, Lombard BTC, Treasury), and 11 Peripheral contracts (Access Manager, Hub Configurator, Spoke Configurator, Config/Giver/Taker Position Managers, Native Token Gateway, Signature Gateway, 3 IR Strategies, and 10 Spoke Oracles). This page is the canonical deployed_contracts_doc.

From https://aave.com/security: 5 V4 audit reports identified — Sherlock collaborative (May 14 2026, Feb 05 2026), ChainSecurity (Feb 19 2026), Trail of Bits (Feb 10 2026), and Blackthorn (Oct 20 2025). Audit PDF URLs are in the aave/aave-v4 GitHub repo at pinned commit e2fb6320d28ed9c6bba66d47f70fed59aef2f64c. No in-scope address tables were extracted from audit PDFs (PDF fetch not attempted with remaining fetch budget); addresses still recorded from D2.

GitHub repo https://github.com/aave/aave-v4 confirmed live; contains scripts/deploy/ and output/ directories consistent with Foundry broadcast artifacts. Internal deployment JSON files (broadcast/run-latest.json or output/*.json) not fetched due to fetch budget constraints. Latest release v0.5.11 dated Mar 20 2026. Repo confirmed as the canonical V4 source repo.

Aave V4 launched exclusively on Ethereum mainnet on March 30, 2026. Multiple sources confirm Ethereum-only deployment at launch, with multi-chain expansion pending Aave DAO governance approval. D5 check: single chain only — no cross-chain enumeration needed.

No factory-pattern contracts identified in the V4 architecture. The protocol uses a fixed set of deployed Hub and Spoke contracts. New Spokes are deployed and registered via governance, not via an on-chain factory enumeration method. No factory children to enumerate.

Role taxonomy applied: Hubs classified as 'vault' (liquidity-holding), Spokes as 'pool' (user-facing borrowing markets), Access Manager as 'admin', Hub Configurator and Spoke Configurator as 'admin', Position Managers as 'router', Gateways as 'router', IR Strategies as 'other', Oracles as 'oracle'. Actor classes set to 'unknown' pending on-chain read verification.

All 25 addresses in admin_addresses[] trace directly to the fetched https://aave.com/docs/resources/addresses page. No snippet-only sightings. AAVE governance token address (0x7fc66500c84a76ad7e9c93437bfc5ac33e2ddae9) and Aave governance forum discovered from secondary sources but not V4 core contracts; recorded in protocol_metadata only.

rationale.verdict: Discovery run walked three corpora — aave.com website, official docs/addresses page, and GitHub repo — plus secondary search results. The official deployments page yielded 25 distinct V4 contract addresses across 3 Hubs, 11 Spokes, and 11 Peripheral contracts, all on Ethereum mainnet. On-chain reads were not performed (no pre-built surfacer URLs provided and fetch budget exhausted), so actor classes and upgradeability remain unknown pending next run.

protocol_metadata.about: Aave V4 is a decentralized, non-custodial lending protocol launched on Ethereum mainnet on March 30, 2026, that allows users to supply assets to earn interest and borrow assets against overcollateralized positions. The protocol introduces a Hub-and-Spoke architecture where Liquidity Hubs consolidate deposited assets into a shared pool while Spokes define independent borrowing markets with their own collateral types, risk parameters, and liquidation rules. This design allows multiple specialized lending environments (e.g., Lido liquid staking e-Mode, Ethena ecosystem, Forex stablecoins, gold-backed assets) to share a single deep liquidity pool without fragmenting capital. Governance is conducted by AAVE token holders via the Aave DAO, which controls supply/borrow caps, Spoke additions, and protocol upgrades.
